A brief heads up before I waste your time with my ramblings: I'm usually more of a lurker these days and my writing skills are rather rusty, so I will appologize in advance for the rambling nature of my posts.

I've always enjoyed online communication starting with forums in my early online years all the way to here. The journey has been rough along the way seeing communities start strong and slowly die off, or burn up quickly in a blaze of fire from within. It's made me reflect on what it was and still is about some of those past communities that made them so great in my eyes.
A few qualities I've narrowed down as important from my perspective are:

  • Meaningful content/Intelligent debate- Saw a lot of this in early forums not so much these days. While it may at times feel like much of the world is often repeating nonsensical falllicies at each other or missinformation they heard from some news source, there have always been places or people who's words break apart from that haze.

  • Whit/humor- This may feel like it's in contrast to the meaninful content point, but I feel like they often go hand in hand. Communities should not try to be overly formal about everything, humour is not always simply a distraction from meaningful conversation but can at times enhance it and make it more digestable/enjoyable. People in communities should make an effort to post factual and accurate information especially in such topics as science/technology etc., but at the same time should remember why we're spending our time on the internet to begin with. (generally to relax or be entertained)

  • Willingness to act/help out- A group of people standing around saying "that thing op posted is boring" or "Hope someone else improves that thing op posted; it's bad it should be good though!", everyone just posting an oppinion and leaving is cool and all but personally I prefer communities that involve themselves in things that they care about when possible.

  • Activeness- This one goes closely along the same lines as the previous but I feel it's disctinct enough to seperate them. Basically, even the best communities need people who still care about what they're about enough to post meaningful things and others who actively read/respond.

Reddit HAD a lot of those qualities, but lately the comments/posts there more greatly ressemble what Facebook or youtube comments are so notoriously associated with.

There is still a large quantity of content on reddit, but the quality has undoubtably gone down. How so? Well there are definately still attempts at humor, but much of the "humorous" content lately consists of reposts or poorly constructed memes. There is still a portion of the community actively trying to help out with causes they believe in, even admins with issues such as net neutrality, but there have been moments when it has seemed as though much of this is done simply because it is expected rather than because they still care. Perhaps I'm overthinking it?

Due to some of the above as well as unmentioned reasons, I've decided I've finally given up on reddit. I see voat as having many of the qualities that I value, while at the same time having the potential to acquire some that it is currently missing. I will remain optimistic of voat's future, while at the same time realizing how far off that idealized future may be.

I apologize again. This is a bit like speaking my thoughts outloud. At the same time, though, this place won't become active if we're all too shy to post. ;p

So, umm. Anyone feel similarly? Perhaps I'm just odd in what I value or view as ideal qualities of communities.
Feels like the time and opportunity to move on is now
